content.intro: This lesson focuses on understanding urls and uris in web networking and http fundamentals. You will connect uniform resource identifier and uniform resource locator to a concrete API contract decision, inspect a small example, and decide what evidence proves the behavior is correct.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding URLs and URIs matters because API consumers depend on predictable behavior even when clients, servers, networks, and stored data evolve independently. Applying uniform resource identifier and uniform resource locator deliberately reduces ambiguity, makes failures easier to diagnose, and gives tests a clear expectation.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: HTTP is the application-layer request/response protocol; message semantics live in methods, status codes, and headers. In this lesson, treat “Understanding URLs and URIs” as a design or implementation decision: name the expected behavior, identify its boundary, and verify it with a representative request or test.

content_blocks.title: Walkthrough
content_blocks.text: Start with “Uniform Resource Identifier and Uniform Resource Locator”; it establishes the vocabulary for this topic. Next, compare it with “Scheme, host, port, path, and query” and “Percent encoding and reserved characters”. In a real API, write down the observable behavior first, then test one normal request and one invalid or unauthorized request. Keep resource state, caller identity, and internal implementation details separate.

common_mistakes: Treating understanding urls and uris as an implementation detail rather than a documented behavior.
Testing only the happy path and ignoring malformed, unauthorized, conflicting, duplicate, or dependency-failure cases.
